statement: Endpoint-shape/common-tangent interface no-go. For every L>=1 set M=2(L!)^2, S=M+1, U=SM, X=[0,S-1], and for e=1,...,L put d_e=Se and A_d={r+dSk:0<=r<d,0<=k<U/d}. Then V=[0,SU-1]=A_d direct-sum dX for every row and U<S^2. All rows have the same round-ten profile Theta=(1/(S-1),1/(S-1),1,1), although their scalar parameters and complement interiors differ. Taking rho=1/2, z_d=d, a common R0>(SL)^2+rho^2, and T_d=R0+A_d-rho^2-d^2 gives positive tangent sets with the common tangent tau0=R0-rho^2, because d^2 belongs to A_d. On tau0 the exact Euclidean chart gives squared target distance (d-d')^2. Thus one shape-profile fibre contains L target positions and exactly L-1 positive distance labels for every L, so no functional map from that endpoint profile alone to the scalar position or common-tangent label set exists. The row count is only L=U^o(1), and selected-core transversality/heavy-factor hypotheses are absent, so the construction does not refute a power-large bridge using those extra hypotheses.
